'''Seymour Dean Van Gundy''' (February 24, 1931 – December 27, 2020) was an American professor emeritus of [[nematology]] at [[University of California, Riverside]] and former dean of the [[College of Agriculture and Natural Resources (UC Riverside)|College of Agriculture and Natural Resources]].

==Background==
After graduating from [[Monclova, Ohio|Monclova]] High School in 1949, Van Gundy attended [[Bowling Green State University]] on an [[Edwin Mosley]] scholarship. While an undergraduate, Van Gundy worked part-time at an [[H.J. Heinz]] research facility. There he met J.C. Walker: a professor teaching at [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]]. Walker offered Van Gundy an assistantship to continue studying cucumbers after Van Gundy's graduation from Bowling Green State University.<ref name="Davis"/> Van Gundy went to University of Wisconsin for graduate work, where he completed his Ph.D. in 1956 and his postdoctoral studies in February 1957. Van Gundy interviewed with Dewey J. Raski for a nematology position at [[University of California, Riverside]] (UCR); Van Gundy was hired by the co-located [[University of California Citrus Experiment Station]] as a junior nematologist in March 1957.<ref name="Davis"/><ref>{{Cite journal|journal=Register - University of California|volume=2|title=Officers and Assistants|publisher=[[University of California Press]]|year=1958|page=266|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9AA5AQAAMAAJ}}</ref>
In 1966 Van Gundy took a sabbatical from teaching to study ''[[Meloidogyne javanica]]'' and ''[[Tylenchulus semipenetrans]]'' in Australia with Harry Wallace and Alan Bird.<ref name="Davis"/><ref>{{Cite journal|journal=[[Australasian Plant Pathology]]|volume=37|issue=3|pages=203–219|publisher=[[Australasian Plant Pathology Society]]|year=2008|url=http://www.appsnet.org/public/history/historynematology.aspx|title=The history of plant and soil nematology in Australia and New Zealand, with particular reference to the contributions of six pioneering nematologists|author1=G. R. Stirling|author2=G. W. Yeates|author3=K. Davies|author4=M. Hodda|doi=10.1071/ap08017|s2cid=34027081|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Van Gundy was promoted to full professor in July 1968.<ref name="Davis"/> In 1969 during the height of the [[Vietnam War]], Van Gundy defended the University's position refusing classified [[United States Department of Defense|Department of Defense]] research projects, citing the restriction against publication counter to the interests of involved graduate and postdoctoral students.<ref>{{Cite news|date=November 20, 1969|newspaper=[[Van Nuys Valley News]]|url=https://newspaperarchive.com/us/california/van-nuys/van-nuys-valley-news/1969/11-20/page-68|page=68|title=University of California, Riverside Refuses to Accept Military Research Endowments|via=[[Newspaperarchive.com]]}}</ref> That same year Van Gundy founded the ''[[Journal of Nematology]]'' for the [[Society of Nematologists]], becoming the journal's first editor-in-chief.<ref>{{Cite journal|journal=Journal of Nematology|date= June 2012|volume=44|issue=2| pmc=3578462 |title=The Society of Nematologists at 50, and Where to from Here?|first=John M.|last=Webster|pages= 107–14|pmid=23482457}}</ref> Beginning in 1970 Van Gundy served as Assistant Vice Chancellor for Research until 1972 when he was recruited by the [[College of Agriculture and Natural Resources (UC Riverside)|College of Agriculture and Natural Resources]]'s dean, [[William Dugger (dean)|William Dugger]], to chair the department of nematology.<ref name="Davis"/>  In 1978, Van Gundy was named a fellow of the [[American Phytopathological Society]].<ref>{{Cite journal|journal=University Bulletin|volume=27|publisher=[[University of California]]|year=1978|title=Elections|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=jvM2AQAAMAAJ}}</ref> Van Gundy continued to chair nematology at UCR until he took a sabbatical in 1984 to study [[rhizobacteria]].<ref name="Davis"/> That work resulted in Van Gundy being awarded a patent for Rhizobacterial plant protection.<ref>{{cite patent|country=US|number=EP 0160089 A1|status=application|title=Rhizobacterial plant protection|pubdate=1985-11-06|gdate=|fdate=1984-10-25|pridate=1983-10-26|invent1=Seymour D. Van Gundy|invent2=Emma Zavaleta-Mejia|assign1=The Regents Of The University Of California}}</ref>

Upon his return he was appointed Associate Dean of Research. Van Gundy was appointed interim dean of the College of Agriculture and Natural Resources in 1988 and became full dean in 1990. He retired in 1993.<ref name="Davis"/><ref>{{Cite journal|title=New agriculture deans for two UC campuses|author1-first=John E.|author1-last=Kinsella|author2-first=Seymour|author2-last=Van Gundy|journal=[[California Agriculture]]|volume=44|issue=3|doi=10.3733/ca.v044n03p4|date=May–June 1990|pages=4–5|url=http://californiaagriculture.ucanr.org/landingpage.cfm?articleid=ca.v044n03p4|doi-access=free}}</ref> Even after retirement he continued to teach courses in growing [[blueberries]] and [[plumeria]]s.<ref>{{Cite news|title=UCR offers class on growing plumerias|date=August 11, 2010|url=http://www.redlandsdailyfacts.com/lifestyle/20100811/ucr-offers-class-on-growing-plumerias|newspaper=Redlands Daily Facts}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Overcome obstacles to cultivating berries|newspaper=[[Redlands Daily Facts]]|date=May 5, 2010|url=https://www.redlandsdailyfacts.com/2010/05/05/overcome-obstacles-to-cultivating-berries/}}</ref> Van Gundy was appointed by Governor [[Gray Davis]] to the Regional Water Quality Control Board for the [[Santa Ana, California|Santa Ana]] region in 2000 and re-appointed by Davis's successor, [[Arnold Schwarzenegger]] in 2006.<ref>{{Cite press release|title=Seymour D. Van Grundy|date=June 2000|url=http://www.fiatlux.ucr.edu/cgi-bin/display.cgi?id=401}}</ref><ref>{{Cite press release|title=UCR Professor Reappointed to State Water Board|date=November 21, 2006|url=http://media-newswire.com/release_1039578.html|publisher=Media-Newswire.com|first=Iqbal|last=Pittalwala}}</ref> In 2006 Van Gundy was inducted by [[Moldova]]'s National Academy of Sciences in thanks of his management of the extension program between UCR and [[Moldova State University]].<ref>{{Cite press release|title=Retired UCR Scientist and Extension Consultant Honored by Moldovan National Academy of Sciences|date=June 12, 2006|url=http://www.extension.ucr.edu/admin/about/pressroom/2006/2006-06-12.html|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402160324/http://www.extension.ucr.edu/admin/about/pressroom/2006/2006-06-12.html|archivedate=April 2, 2015}}</ref>
